meta.title: The Caro Playbook — Where we are, where we're going
meta.description: Caro's founder-arc stage map adapted from Anthropic's Founder's Playbook. We're at late MVP heading into Launch. The next gate is retention, not features.

hero.title: Where Caro is on the founder arc
hero.subtitle: We adapted Anthropic's Founder's Playbook into a stage map you can actually inspect — with the evidence, the gaps, and the honest failure modes we're watching for.

intro.heading: Why we publish this
intro.body: Most companies tell you they have product-market fit. We tell you the four-stage map we're on, where we sit on it, and what evidence we'd need to claim the next stage. The playbook came from Anthropic; the honesty is the only way to make it useful.

idea.title: Stage 1 — Idea
idea.summary: Problem validated. Personas documented. Distribution channels live. Waitlist signal is real (~247) but qualitative — quantitative validation gates are codified now to apply forward from May 25, 2026.
idea.evidence: MISSION.md, docs/PERSONAS_JTBD.md, docs/JOBS_TO_BE_DONE.md, live waitlist on caro.sh

mvp.title: Stage 2 — MVP
mvp.summary: Core loop ships at 94.8% Command Success Rate. Multi-backend by construction (no single-vendor lock-in). 52+ dangerous-command patterns. 700+ eval cases. Engineering discipline encoded in a tiered constitution.

launch.title: Stage 3 — Launch
launch.summary: Distribution shipped (crates.io, Homebrew, npm, NuGet, install script). Public surface shipped (15-locale website, docs). The exit gate is retention, not features. Until we publish a defended D7 curve, we do not claim PMF.
launch.evidence: Multi-channel distribution, telemetry infrastructure, docs/retention-dashboard-spec.md (spec only; dashboard not yet shipped)

scale.title: Stage 4 — Scale
scale.summary: Dual-track Community / Enterprise per ADR-001. Multi-agent operating layer in place (Hermes + 33 domain agents). Scale is horizontal adoption inside orgs that already deploy AI coding agents — not consumer pivots.

discipline.heading: The five gates we now apply to ourselves
discipline.body: Adopting the playbook meant codifying its anti-confirmation-bias practices as a constitution rule. New product lines clear five gates before the spec graduates from research to implementation.

gates.name: 20 first-hand transcripts
gates.body: Real interviews, not surveys, not stars, not waitlist counts. 20 conversations surfacing at least 3 distinct pain patterns.

gates.name: No surveys as primary evidence
gates.body: Surveys size hypotheses after qualitative interviews surface them — never replace them.

gates.name: What breaks at 100 real users
gates.body: Every spec names the demoware-trap failure mode and the instrumentation that would detect it.

gates.name: Devil's-advocate review
gates.body: An adversarial agent interrogates AI-drafted proposals before merge to counter confirmation bias.

gates.name: Sean Ellis with a defended cohort
gates.body: PMF claims require both the >40% threshold and a cohort definition we can defend — not 'everyone who installed'.

audit.heading: We audited our own roadmap against these gates
audit.body: Five v2.0 product lines moved to Research (unvalidated) because they had zero first-hand transcripts: Karo distributed intelligence, Dogma rule engine, voice synthesis, self-healing, and local context indexing. The four items that extend the already-validated core loop (Azure Foundry, vLLM Jukebox, Skills extension, Handy.Computer) pass as extensions and remain on v2.0.
